sub_genres.label: Classic / Traditional RTS
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Resource gathering, base construction, tech-tree progression, and producing armies.
sub_genres.examples: StarCraft II, Age of Empires IV, Command & Conquer
sub_genres.engine_note: Needs deterministic lockstep or tight server authority; Godot (NavigationServer3D + C#) and Unreal (Mass Entity) both work well at 100-300 unit caps.

sub_genres.label: Real-Time Tactics (RTT)
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Focuses on positioning, cover systems, line-of-sight, and unit abilities with minimal base building.
sub_genres.examples: Company of Heroes 3, Dawn of War II
sub_genres.engine_note: Lower unit counts favor higher visual fidelity and destructible cover (Unreal Chaos Destruction + GAS).

sub_genres.label: Grand Strategy & Large-Scale Warfare
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Massive maps, thousands of simultaneous units, strategic zoom, and supply-line logistics.
sub_genres.examples: Supreme Commander, Beyond All Reason, Hegemony
sub_genres.engine_note: CPU/draw-call bound; requires MultiMeshInstance3D + C++/GDExtension in Godot or Mass Entity + Niagara instancing in Unreal.

sub_genres.label: Survival & Tower Defense / Attack
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Holding out against escalating waves, fortifying choke points, or pushing enemy nodes.
sub_genres.examples: They Are Billions, Creeper World, Rogue Command
sub_genres.engine_note: Flow-field pathfinding replaces per-unit A*; Godot lightweight 2D/3D servers make rapid prototyping fast.

sub_genres.label: RPG-Hybrid & Hero RTS
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Army control paired with hero units that gain XP, equip items, and cast active abilities.
sub_genres.examples: Warcraft III, Godsworn, SpellForce 3
sub_genres.engine_note: Requires a robust ability/buff framework (Unreal GAS or Godot Resource-driven ability nodes).

sub_genres.label: Space & 3D Movement RTS
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Full 3D combat with vertical maneuvering, fleet formations, and spherical sensor ranges.
sub_genres.examples: Homeworld, Sins of a Solar Empire II
sub_genres.engine_note: Replaces 2D navmeshes with 3D octree/boids steering and orbital camera controllers.

sub_genres.label: 4X (Explore, Expand, Exploit, Exterminate)
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Empire-scale management across hex/tile maps with diplomacy, research trees, and economic snowballing.
sub_genres.examples: Civilization VI, Old World, Age of Wonders 4
sub_genres.engine_note: Heavy UI and data-table management; Godot Control nodes and TileMapLayer keep iteration snappy.

sub_genres.label: Tactical RPG / SRPG
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Squad combat on a discrete grid with action points, flanking, elevation, and persistent builds.
sub_genres.examples: XCOM 2, Into the Breach, Fire Emblem
sub_genres.engine_note: Needs clean grid-state serialization and camera transitions (Godot AStarGrid2D or Unreal DataAssets + Sequencer).

sub_genres.label: Deckbuilder & Card Strategy
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Drafting, pruning, and playing cards to manage energy, synergies, and RNG.
sub_genres.examples: Slay the Spire, Monster Train, Balatro
sub_genres.engine_note: Almost entirely UI, tweening, and state-machine logic; strongly Godot-favored for fast 2D/UI iteration.

sub_genres.label: Operational Wargame
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Military hex grids emphasizing supply lines, terrain modifiers, and combined-arms doctrine.
sub_genres.examples: Panzer Corps 2, Unity of Command II
sub_genres.engine_note: Data-driven rulesets with minimal 3D overhead; ideal for Godot 2D/2.5D.

sub_genres.label: First-Person Shooter (FPS)
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Direct first-person aiming, weapon handling, movement tech, and spatial map control.
sub_genres.examples: DOOM Eternal, Counter-Strike 2, Titanfall 2
sub_genres.engine_note: Unreal-favored for multiplayer prediction/lag compensation; Godot excels for single-player/boomer shooters.

sub_genres.label: Third-Person Shooter (TPS)
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Over-the-shoulder aiming, cover mechanics, dodge rolls, and character animation blending.
sub_genres.examples: Helldivers 2, Gears of War, Remnant II
sub_genres.engine_note: Unreal Motion Matching and CharacterMovementComponent give a head start for complex locomotion.

sub_genres.label: Hack-and-Slash / Character Action
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Fast-paced melee combos, cancel windows, crowd control, and combat rankings.
sub_genres.examples: Devil May Cry 5, Bayonetta, Hades
sub_genres.engine_note: Requires frame-accurate hitboxes, hitstop, and animation-driven state machines.

sub_genres.label: Soulslike / Deliberate Melee
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Stamina management, telegraphed patterns, i-frame dodging, parrying, and high-stakes checkpoints.
sub_genres.examples: Elden Ring, Lies of P, Sekiro
sub_genres.engine_note: Relies heavily on root-motion animations and tight animation-notify windows (Unreal AnimMontages or Godot AnimationTree).

sub_genres.label: Stealth
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Light/sound detection systems, AI patrol states, disguises, and silent takedowns.
sub_genres.examples: Hitman, Dishonored, Metal Gear Solid V
sub_genres.engine_note: Driven by AI perception cones, sound propagation, and dynamic lighting queries.

sub_genres.label: Bullet Hell / Survivors-like
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Dodging dense projectile patterns or swarms while auto-firing or twin-stick aiming.
sub_genres.examples: Vampire Survivors, Enter the Gungeon, Touhou
sub_genres.engine_note: Bypass standard physics bodies for thousands of bullets; use Godot PhysicsServer2D / MultiMeshInstance2D.

sub_genres.label: Precision 2D Platformer
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Frame-tight jumping, air dashes, coyote time, and instant respawns across hazard screens.
sub_genres.examples: Celeste, Super Meat Boy
sub_genres.engine_note: Godot native 2D pixel-coordinate engine and CharacterBody2D are purpose-built for this.

sub_genres.label: Metroidvania
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Interconnected non-linear exploration gated by permanent movement and combat upgrades.
sub_genres.examples: Hollow Knight, Ori, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown
sub_genres.engine_note: Requires seamless room streaming/transitions and persistent world-state flags.

sub_genres.label: 3D Collectathon / Mascot Platformer
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Expressive 3D movement across open sandbox levels to gather collectibles.
sub_genres.examples: Super Mario Odyssey, Astro Bot, A Hat in Time
sub_genres.engine_note: Needs shadow-blob indicators, spring-arm cameras, and custom gravity/slope handling.

sub_genres.label: Cinematic / Puzzle Platformer
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Physics-driven traversal focused on atmosphere, environmental hazards, and visual storytelling.
sub_genres.examples: Inside, Little Nightmares, Limbo
sub_genres.engine_note: Heavy emphasis on lighting, post-processing, and scripted physics triggers.

sub_genres.label: Isometric Action RPG (ARPG)
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Fast top-down combat, randomized loot tables, skill trees, and dungeon grinding.
sub_genres.examples: Diablo IV, Path of Exile 2, Grim Dawn
sub_genres.engine_note: Needs scalable stat-modifier pipelines and procedural level stitching.

sub_genres.label: CRPG (Computer / Narrative RPG)
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Party exploration, branching dialogue trees, skill checks, and tactical combat.
sub_genres.examples: Baldur's Gate 3, Disco Elysium, Divinity: OS 2
sub_genres.engine_note: Dialogue/quest graph tooling and save-state serialization are the primary bottlenecks.

sub_genres.label: Open-World Action RPG
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Large seamless worlds with freeform exploration, questlines, factions, and real-time combat.
sub_genres.examples: The Witcher 3, Skyrim, Cyberpunk 2077
sub_genres.engine_note: Unreal World Partition, Nanite, and PCG give a decisive edge at AA/AAA scale.

sub_genres.label: JRPG (Turn-Based / Party-Driven)
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Structured narrative arcs, party roles, elemental weaknesses, and menu/active-time battles.
sub_genres.examples: Persona 5 Royal, Sea of Stars, Octopath Traveler II
sub_genres.engine_note: Heavily UI- and cutscene-driven; Godot excels for 2D/HD-2D, Unreal for high-budget 3D.

sub_genres.label: Roguelike / Roguelite
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Procedural runs, permadeath, build-defining relics/synergies, and meta-progression.
sub_genres.examples: Dead Cells, The Binding of Isaac, Caves of Qud
sub_genres.engine_note: Modular room/chunk generation and decoupled modifier systems are key.

sub_genres.label: Creature Collector / Monster Tamer
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Capturing, training, evolving, and battling with a roster of distinct creatures.
sub_genres.examples: Pokemon, Palworld, Cassette Beasts
sub_genres.engine_note: Relies on clean data-driven species databases (Godot Resources, Unreal DataTables).

sub_genres.label: City Builder
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Zoning, infrastructure networks (roads, power, water), citizen happiness, and municipal economics.
sub_genres.examples: Cities: Skylines, Frostpunk, Manor Lords
sub_genres.engine_note: Spline-based networks and agent traffic require decoupled simulation threads.

sub_genres.label: Colony Sim / Base Management
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Indirect control of autonomous agents via job priorities, survival needs, and emergent stories.
sub_genres.examples: RimWorld, Dwarf Fortress, Oxygen Not Included
sub_genres.engine_note: Utility AI / GOAP task schedulers and grid-based gas/temperature/pathing maps.

sub_genres.label: Automation & Factory Sim
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Extracting raw materials and building interlocking belts, pipes, and machines for throughput.
sub_genres.examples: Factorio, Satisfactory, Dyson Sphere Program
sub_genres.engine_note: Items on belts must be simulated as pure data arrays, never individual physics objects.

sub_genres.label: Life & Farming Sim
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Daily time-of-day loops, crop cycles, crafting, decorating, and NPC schedules.
sub_genres.examples: Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, Coral Island
sub_genres.engine_note: Driven by calendar/clock singletons, inventory grids, and NPC schedule tables.

sub_genres.label: Vehicle, Flight & Physics Sim
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Realistic aerodynamics, suspension, orbital mechanics, or soft-body physics modeling.
sub_genres.examples: Microsoft Flight Simulator, BeamNG.drive, Kerbal Space Program
sub_genres.engine_note: Requires high-frequency fixed physics ticks (Unreal Chaos Vehicles or custom C++ physics).

sub_genres.label: Survival Horror
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Scarce resources, inventory constraints, vulnerable protagonists, and tension-building atmosphere.
sub_genres.examples: Resident Evil 4, Silent Hill 2, Signalis
sub_genres.engine_note: Lighting and audio carry the experience (Unreal Lumen/MetaSounds or Godot retro/2D).

sub_genres.label: Open-World Survival Craft
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Gathering resources, managing hunger/temperature, building shelters, and biome progression.
sub_genres.examples: Subnautica, Valheim, Minecraft
sub_genres.engine_note: Needs voxel or modular snap-building, terrain streaming, and persistent multiplayer saves.

sub_genres.label: Narrative / Walking Sim
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Minimal combat; focuses on environmental storytelling, dialogue, and atmospheric exploration.
sub_genres.examples: Firewatch, Edith Finch, Outer Wilds
sub_genres.engine_note: Relies on trigger volumes, audio logs, and seamless camera/animation scripting.

sub_genres.label: Point-and-Click / Detective
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Inspecting scenes, combining inventory items, interrogating suspects, and logical deduction.
sub_genres.examples: Return of the Obra Dinn, Golden Idol, Monkey Island
sub_genres.engine_note: Strongly Godot-favored due to simple 2D/3D raycast interaction and rich UI/text support.

sub_genres.label: Spatial / Sokoban Grid Puzzle
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Discrete grid movement where every step alters the board state, often with rule-bending mechanics.
sub_genres.examples: Baba Is You, Stephen's Sausage Roll
sub_genres.engine_note: Pure deterministic state-stack for instant undo/redo; ideal for Godot.

sub_genres.label: First-Person Environmental Puzzle
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Manipulating 3D world mechanics (portals, lasers, time loops, perspective) in test chambers.
sub_genres.examples: Portal 2, The Witness, The Talos Principle 2
sub_genres.engine_note: Requires clean custom shader/render-target pipelines and rock-solid physics interactions.

sub_genres.label: Physics & Contraption Puzzle
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Building structures or triggering chain reactions governed by rigid-body gravity and momentum.
sub_genres.examples: Poly Bridge, World of Goo, Bad Piggies
sub_genres.engine_note: Deterministic physics stepping (Jolt in Godot or Chaos in Unreal) so solutions stay consistent.

sub_genres.label: Match-3 & Rhythm
sub_genres.how_it_plays: Pattern recognition under move limits or timed inputs synced to an audio track.
sub_genres.examples: Candy Crush, Crypt of the NecroDancer, Hi-Fi RUSH
sub_genres.engine_note: Rhythm games require audio-clock DSP sync (Godot AudioServer, Unreal Quartz).
